The Counterparty acknowledges this disclaimer and shall not represent the Company as a custodian, broker-dealer, settlement agent or guarantor.
redflags:
Commingling of Customer Assets with counterparty proprietary funds.
Counterparty may impose liens, rehypothecate or reuse Customer Assets without written approval.
Reconciliation delayed beyond 24 hours for material discrepancies.
No segregation, key management or wallet access controls.
Counterparty or platform represents [Company] as custodian, adviser or asset guarantor.
usageNotes:
Always escalate to Legal, Compliance and Finance for any arrangement involving Customer Assets, Digital Assets, gold, wallets, private keys or settlement infrastructure.
BAPPEBTI (Indonesia), MAS (Singapore) and equivalent regulators impose strict asset segregation and safeguarding requirements. External counsel review is mandatory for regulated custody arrangements.
counselNotes: Narrower asset provisions may be accepted only where: (a) there is no access to, control over, transfer of or settlement responsibility for Customer Assets; (b) the Company's role is solely informational or technology-provisioning; and (c) Legal and Compliance have confirmed that no custody, settlement or regulated-asset characterisation applies.

title: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY OWNERSHIP
purpose: Allocates ownership of pre-existing IP and newly created work.
baseline: Intellectual Property Ownership. Each Party retains ownership of its pre-existing Intellectual Property Rights. Except as expressly stated in this Agreement, no right, title, interest or licence in either Party's Intellectual Property Rights is transferred or licensed by implication, estoppel, operation of law or otherwise.
buyside:
Ownership of Deliverables (Company).
(a) All Deliverables specifically created for the Company under this Agreement (including work product, reports, code, configurations, integrations, documentation, data models and analysis) shall be owned by the Company on creation as a work made for hire to the fullest extent permitted by law; where that characterisation is not available, the Counterparty hereby irrevocably assigns to the Company all rights in such Deliverables, including copyright, database rights, patent rights and all other Intellectual Property Rights. The Counterparty shall execute any documents required to perfect or record the assignment at the Company's request.
(b) Where the Counterparty incorporates its pre-existing Intellectual Property Rights into a Deliverable, the Counterparty grants the Company a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence to use that background IP to the extent necessary to use, maintain and exploit the Deliverable.
sellside: Company IP Retained. The Company retains all rights in its Platform, software, data, algorithms, models, documentation, feedback, roadmap, enhancements and derivative works. The Counterparty receives only the limited licence expressly granted in Clause [●] (Licence Rights) during the Term. Any feedback or suggestions provided by the Counterparty relating to the Company's Platform or Services shall be owned by the Company without restriction.
fallback: Licence in Lieu of Assignment. Where vendor ownership of bespoke Deliverables is commercially unavoidable, the Counterparty grants the Company a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive licence to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works from and sub-licence the Deliverables for the Company's internal and commercial purposes.
redflags:
Vendor owns bespoke work paid for by [Company] without granting a perpetual, irrevocable licence.
Implied licence only — no express grant.
Vendor may reuse [Company]-confidential requirements, data, product design or custom features for competitors.
Feedback or improvement suggestions automatically become vendor IP.
usageNotes:
IP assignment formalities differ by jurisdiction. In Indonesia, copyright assignment requires written agreement. In India and Philippines, moral rights may apply to certain creative works. Confirm with local counsel.
For AI, machine learning or co-developed technology, document IP ownership separately at SOW level before commencement.
counselNotes: Accept a licence in lieu of assignment only where vendor ownership of bespoke Deliverables is commercially unavoidable; otherwise require assignment under the Buy-Side provision.

title: LICENCE RIGHTS
purpose: Defines permitted use of IP, platform and materials.
baseline: Licence Rights. Any licence granted under this Agreement is: (a) limited to the Permitted Purpose and scope expressly stated; (b) non-exclusive, unless stated otherwise; (c) non-transferable and non-sublicensable without the Company's written consent; (d) revocable on the terms of this Agreement; and (e) subject to all stated terms, conditions and restrictions. No right, title or interest is conveyed except as expressly stated.
buyside: Licence to the Company. The Counterparty grants the Company a worldwide, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the Deliverables and the Counterparty's background Intellectual Property Rights as embedded in the Deliverables, to the extent necessary for the Company to exploit, maintain, modify and sub-licence the Deliverables for its business purposes.
sellside: Licence to the Counterparty. The Company grants the Counterparty a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, revocable licence to access and use the Company's Platform solely for the Permitted Purpose during the Term, subject to: (a) compliance with the Company's acceptable-use policy and technical documentation; (b) payment of all applicable Fees; and (c) immediate revocation on breach, termination or suspension. The Counterparty shall not sub-licence, resell, transfer or grant access to the Company's Platform to any third party without the Company's express written approval.
redflags:
Perpetual, unrestricted, transferable or sublicensable licence to [Company] brand, data, platform, algorithms, models or documentation.
Licence that survives termination for conduct not expressly agreed.
Counterparty may sublicence [Company] materials to third parties without consent.
usageNotes: Licence scope must match the actual integration and use case. Do not accept broad licences in template agreements without verifying that the scope matches reality.
counselNotes: Accept a broader licence scope only where: (a) it is commercially priced and the risk has been specifically assessed; (b) it is limited to the Company's internal business purposes; and (c) it is no broader than necessary for the specific use case documented in the Statement of Work.

title: WORK PRODUCT, DEVELOPMENTS, CUSTOMISATIONS AND FEEDBACK
purpose: Controls rights in project outputs and improvements.
baseline: Work Product, Developments and Feedback. All Deliverables specifically created for the Company under this Agreement shall be owned by the Company on creation or, if earlier, on full payment of the relevant Fees, as specified in the applicable Statement of Work. The Counterparty shall identify any background Intellectual Property Rights embedded in a Deliverable in the applicable Statement of Work.
buyside:
Enhanced Work-Product Obligations. The Counterparty shall:
(a) deliver all source code, assets, documentation and materials forming part of the Deliverables to the Company on acceptance;
(b) obtain and waive, to the extent permitted by law, any moral rights in the Deliverables on behalf of its personnel; and
(c) not use the Company's confidential requirements, designs, data models, specifications or product roadmap in deliverables for any other customer.
sellside: Feedback. All feedback, suggestions, ideas and improvements provided by the Counterparty relating to the Company's Platform, services or products are assigned to the Company without restriction. The Company may improve, commercialise or modify its Platform based on that feedback without obligation or payment to the Counterparty.
redflags:
Vendor owns bespoke, [Company]-specific deliverables paid for by [Company].
No source code delivery for custom-built integrations or platform-critical code.
Vendor may reuse [Company] confidential requirements, design concepts or product features for other customers.
usageNotes: Ensure each SOW clearly identifies: (a) what [Company] owns; (b) what vendor owns; and (c) the licence scope for each. Generic SOW language creates IP disputes post-delivery.
counselNotes: Accept vendor ownership of underlying tools or frameworks only where: (a) the Company receives a broad, irrevocable licence for the specific use case; (b) the tool or framework is identified as vendor IP in the Statement of Work; and (c) the tool is not specific to the Company and is available to the vendor's other customers.

title: OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE
purpose: Prevents copyleft contamination and licence breach.
baseline: Open-Source Software. The Counterparty shall not include open-source software in any Deliverable in a manner that would require: (a) the disclosure, licensing or transfer of the Company's proprietary source code, data or materials; (b) restrictions on the Company's ability to charge for the Deliverable or its derivatives; or (c) the application of any copyleft, share-alike or similar licence to the Company's proprietary materials.
sellside: Company-Supplied Open Source. Where the Company provides software or platform access containing open-source components, the Counterparty shall comply with all applicable open-source licence notices provided by the Company. The Counterparty shall not reverse engineer the Company's proprietary software or extract the Company's code from any delivered component.
redflags:
Undisclosed copyleft (GPL, LGPL, AGPL) open-source embedded in Deliverables.
No open-source inventory or licence compliance warranty.
No security scanning or vulnerability remediation for open-source dependencies.
usageNotes: For software development, AI model training and platform integration contracts, open-source compliance is a mandatory diligence step. Engage Engineering for OSS scanning before acceptance.
counselNotes: Permissive open-source (e.g. MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD) may be accepted only if disclosed in the open-source inventory and confirmed not to contaminate the Company's proprietary code.

title: AI TOOLS AND AUTOMATED PROCESSING
purpose: Controls use of AI tools with [Company] data, brand, IP and regulated content.
baseline: AI Tools and Automated Processing. The Counterparty shall not use, input, upload, expose or make available the Company's Confidential Information, Personal Data, Customer Assets data, Intellectual Property Rights, content, materials or trade secrets to any artificial-intelligence tool, large language model, generative-AI system or machine-learning algorithm without the Company's prior written approval in each case.
sellside: Company AI Outputs. Where the Company provides AI-assisted or automated outputs as part of the Services, the Company disclaims liability for outcomes based on AI outputs that are: (a) used for legal, investment, tax, regulated or medical decision-making without independent professional review; or (b) inconsistent with the Counterparty's specific circumstances not disclosed to the Company. The Counterparty shall independently verify all AI-assisted outputs before relying on them.
redflags:
AI training on [Company] data, Personal Data, Confidential Information or IP without written approval.
Unreviewed AI outputs used for regulated decisions, customer communications, legal advice or investment recommendations.
No AI tools register or disclosure obligation.
usageNotes: AI regulation is evolving rapidly. This is a prudent internal control. Review AI clauses at each annual playbook update in light of applicable AI regulations in [Company] jurisdictions.
counselNotes: Limited AI use may be accepted only if: (a) no Personal Data or Confidential Information is processed by the AI tool; (b) all outputs are human-reviewed before use; and (c) the AI tool is identified and approved by the Company in writing.

title: CONFIDENTIALITY
purpose: Protects non-public information and restricts unauthorised disclosure.
baseline:
Confidentiality.
(a) Each Party shall: (i) keep all Confidential Information received from the other Party strictly confidential; (ii) use it only for the purposes of this Agreement; and (iii) disclose it only to its officers, employees, directors, advisers and subcontractors who need to know and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Clause.
(b) Each Party shall notify the other immediately on becoming aware of any breach of this Clause.
(c) This Clause survives termination of this Agreement indefinitely for trade secrets and for [five (5)] years for other Confidential Information, unless the Parties agree otherwise.
sellside: Company Confidentiality Limitation. The Company's confidentiality obligations are limited to information clearly marked as confidential, or which a reasonable party would understand to be confidential given the context. The Company may disclose Confidential Information to its Affiliates, advisers, Regulators, legal counsel, auditors and service providers on a need-to-know basis without consent, subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.
fallback: Fixed Survival Period. This Clause survives termination for [three (3)] years in respect of ordinary business Confidential Information; trade secrets, security information, customer data and Personal Data remain protected indefinitely.
redflags:
Broad permission to use [Company] Confidential Information for benchmarking, competitive intelligence, AI training, marketing or product development.
No return or destruction obligation on termination.
No injunctive relief available for breach.
No survival clause — confidentiality expires on termination.
usageNotes:
For regulated entities, regulators may require disclosure of certain information. Ensure compelled disclosure carve-out includes advance notice to [Company] where law permits.
Confidentiality obligations in NDA should align with those in the main agreement. Check for conflicts.
counselNotes: A fixed [three (3)]-year survival period is acceptable for ordinary business information, but trade secrets, security information, customer data and Personal Data must remain protected indefinitely.

title: PUBLICITY, ANNOUNCEMENTS, TRADEMARKS AND MARKETING REFERENCES
purpose: Controls public use of [Company] name and brand.
baseline: Publicity, Announcements and Trademarks. Neither Party may issue any press release, public announcement, marketing material, social-media post, website content or investor communication that uses the other Party's name, logo, trademark, trade name, brand, products or relationship without prior written approval, except as required by law. Where disclosure is required by law, the disclosing Party shall give the other as much advance notice as reasonably practicable.
sellside: Company Marketing References. The Company may identify the Counterparty as a customer or partner in the Company's factual marketing materials where commercially appropriate, subject to this Agreement. The Counterparty may not use the Company's brand or name in any context that could imply the Company's endorsement, warranty or regulatory status.
fallback: Approved Announcement. A Party may issue a single public announcement of the relationship using text approved in advance in writing by the other Party's Legal and Communications functions, provided that no regulatory status, endorsement or investment claim is made.
redflags:
Counterparty uses [Company] name, logo or brand in pitch decks, websites, investor materials, regulatory submissions or social media without prior written approval.
Counterparty implies [Company] endorsement, regulatory approval, exclusivity or investment backing.
usageNotes: Brand controls are critical for regulated financial services where counterparty communications may create regulatory risk or customer confusion. Always coordinate with Comms and Compliance before any public announcement.

title: NON-EXCLUSIVITY
purpose: Preserves [Company] strategic flexibility.
baseline: Non-Exclusivity. This Agreement is non-exclusive. Nothing in it restricts or limits the Company from appointing, engaging, developing internally, acquiring or using any third party, alternative service provider, competing product, alternative solution or internal capability for the same or similar purpose, whether before, during or after the Term.
buyside:
Enhanced Non-Exclusivity. In addition to the Baseline:
(a) the Company retains the right to build, acquire or develop any competing or alternative capability without restriction;
(b) no minimum volume, minimum spend, preferred-supplier status, most-favoured-customer right or referral obligation applies to the Company unless expressly stated in Schedule [●]; and
(c) the Company's use or non-use of the Counterparty's Services shall not create any obligation or estoppel.
sellside: Company Freedom to Compete. Nothing in this Agreement restricts the Company's right to offer the same or similar products, services or platform capabilities to any third party. The Company may serve competitors of the Counterparty and is not restricted in the development, marketing or provision of competing products.
fallback: Limited Exclusivity. For a period of [X] months from the Effective Date, the Company shall not engage [defined category] services from the named direct competitors listed in Schedule [●], provided that: (a) the exclusivity is limited to a precisely defined scope; (b) the Company retains full termination-for-convenience rights; and (c) the exclusivity expires automatically on [specified date or trigger].
redflags:
Broad exclusivity, de facto exclusivity through volume commitments or category restrictions.
Competitor restrictions that limit [Company] business or acquisition activities.
Minimum volumes or preferred status without approved business case and Documented Approval.
usageNotes: Exclusivity, MFN and minimum commitment arrangements are Escalation Required. Do not agree commercially without Head of Legal, Finance and Business owner sign-off.
counselNotes: Accept limited exclusivity only with Head of Legal and business-owner approval, and only where the scope is precisely defined, the Company keeps termination-for-convenience rights, and the restriction expires automatically.

title: EXCLUSIVITY, MFN, MINIMUM COMMITMENTS AND VOLUME COMMITMENTS
purpose: Controls strategic and financial lock-in.
baseline: Exclusivity, MFN and Minimum Commitments. No exclusivity, most-favoured-customer undertaking, minimum purchase, minimum volume, minimum revenue commitment, preferred-supplier status, preferred-pricing right, right of first refusal, right of first offer or similar restriction applies to the Company unless expressly approved in writing by the Company and stated in Schedule [●] (Commercial Terms).
buyside: Protective Conditions for Any Restriction. Where any exclusivity, MFN, minimum commitment or volume guarantee is commercially unavoidable, it shall include: (a) a scope limited to a precisely defined product, service or geography; (b) a maximum term of [X] months; (c) measurable performance conditions before the restriction applies; (d) automatic termination of the restriction if the Counterparty fails to meet agreed KPIs; and (e) the Company's unconditional right to terminate the restriction for regulatory reasons.
sellside: No Company Commitment. The Counterparty acknowledges that the Company makes no commitment as to volumes, referrals, allocations or preferred status under this Agreement unless expressly stated. Nothing obliges the Company to purchase minimum volumes or to meet any revenue target.
fallback: Pilot Minimum Spend. The Company commits to a minimum spend of [USD X] during the pilot period of [X] months, subject to: (a) the Counterparty meeting all Service Levels; and (b) the Company's right to terminate for convenience on [thirty (30)] days' notice during the pilot period.
redflags:
Open-ended exclusivity without defined scope, term, KPIs or termination right.
MFN with audit rights over [Company] pricing across other customers.
Minimum spend commitment that continues beyond contract term or if Counterparty fails to perform.
Volume commitments without aligned performance conditions or exit rights.
usageNotes: Exclusivity, MFN and minimum commitments are always Escalation Required. Business teams must not agree these commercially without Head of Legal, Finance and business owner approval in advance.
counselNotes: Accept a minimum commitment only where unavoidable (e.g. pilot arrangements) and only with the conditions above; otherwise the Company gives no minimum or exclusivity commitment.

title: NON-SOLICITATION, NON-CIRCUMVENTION AND RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS
purpose: Protects relationships while avoiding unenforceable overbreadth.
baseline: Non-Solicitation. During the Term and for [twelve (12)] months after termination or expiry, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment, hire or engage (whether as employee, contractor or consultant) any personnel of the other Party who was directly involved in performing this Agreement, except through general public advertisements not specifically targeted at such personnel.
buyside: Non-Circumvention (Strategic Partnerships). For strategic partnerships involving significant investment, proprietary information sharing or customer introductions, the Counterparty shall not, during the Term and for [twenty-four (24)] months thereafter, directly or indirectly approach, solicit or seek to divert from the Company any customer, prospect, supplier or referral source identified to the Counterparty specifically in connection with this Agreement, without the Company's prior written consent.
sellside: Company Restriction Limited. The Company is bound only by the mutual non-solicitation in Clause [●] (Non-Solicitation). The Company does not accept any non-compete, non-circumvention, customer non-solicitation or market restriction that would limit its ability to conduct its ordinary business, serve existing or future customers, or make acquisitions.
redflags:
Broad non-compete that restricts [Company] from operating in any market, product category or geography.
Indefinite non-circumvention without defined scope or duration.
Non-solicit that restricts [Company] from engaging customers not introduced under this Agreement.
Penalties or liquidated damages for breach of non-compete that are disproportionate.
usageNotes:
Enforceability of non-compete and non-solicit obligations varies materially: Indonesia — generally unenforceable without consideration; Singapore — courts apply restraint of trade analysis; India — largely unenforceable post-employment under s.27 Indian Contract Act; Philippines — context-specific.
Always flag restrictive covenants to Head of Legal for review.
counselNotes: Accept only a narrow employee non-solicitation tied to named or directly-involved personnel, for a period not exceeding [twelve (12)] months after termination; do not accept customer non-solicitation or non-compete restrictions on the Company.

title: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES - FUNDAMENTAL
purpose: Confirms the counterparty is a legally existing entity with authority to bind itself contractually. These representations address contract enforceability, not performance capability. If a counterparty cannot give these representations cleanly, the contract may be void or voidable regardless of commercial terms. Any qualification, hedge, or refusal to provide these representations is a material red flag requiring immediate disclosure of the underlying issue and escalation to Head of Legal. Legiti
redflags:
[Counterparty] qualifies or declines any representation without full written disclosure.
[Counterparty] proposes knowledge qualification for legal existence, authority or signatory authorization.
Board authorization stated as "pending" but execution proposed immediately.
Signatory identified only by given name, title or role, or authority shown as limited or conditional.
Disclosure of pending litigation, insolvency, regulatory investigation or enforcement affecting legal capacity.
Entity name, jurisdiction or status unverified against corporate registry.
Constitutional documents restrict or prohibit transaction type, value, term or jurisdiction.
usageNotes: This clause is mandatory for every contract regardless of value, term, transaction type, counterparty or commercial context without exception; even routine, low-value vendor contracts require Clause 35 representations in unqualified form. Before or at signature, request all three of the following: (i) certificate of incorporation or good standing from corporate registry; (ii) certified board resolution authorizing this Agreement and naming signatories by full legal name, or certified power of attorney, or other evidence acceptable to Legal; and (iii) constitutional documents (articles of association, bylaws or equivalent) showing no restriction on authority. Jurisdiction-specific requirements: Indonesia (certified notarized deed and NIB), Singapore (ACRA certificate plus certified board resolution), Philippines (SEC certificate plus certified board resolution), India (RoC certificate plus certified board resolution plus PAN). If counterparty cannot provide documentary evidence, do not sign; instead request written statement explaining which evidence cannot be provided, why (factual and legal reasons), underlying issue (litigation, board dispute, insolvency, regulatory prohibition), and proposed alternative evidence, then escalate immediately to Legal with counterparty's statement. If counterparty qualifies or hedges any representation, stop and do not proceed: unacceptable qualifications include "to our knowledge, we are duly incorporated" (legal existence is absolute fact, not knowledge-qualified), "board approval is pending" (cannot sign until finalized), "we believe the signatory has authority" (authority must be confirmed, not believed); borderline qualifications such as "entry does not violate law except as disclosed in Schedule X" require escalation to Legal (disclosure may be acceptable if immaterial or being remedied). Default rule: if uncertain, require all documentary evidence and escalate before proceeding.

title: BUSINESS AND COOPERATION REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
purpose: These representations address operational capability, regulatory compliance and performance quality. They allocate risk as between Parties for matters within [Counterparty]'s knowledge and control: regulatory status, compliance with law, quality and fitness of services, technical capability, conflicts and adverse proceedings. Unlike Clause 35 (invariably required unqualified), these may be negotiated according to transaction risk, leverage, value and criticality. Performance warranties for secur
sellside: Company Warranties (Limited). The Company's warranties are limited to: (i) the Services being performed with reasonable skill and care in accordance with industry standards; and (ii) Company-provided materials not infringing third-party Intellectual Property Rights (excluding third-party content, open-source software and customer materials). The Company does not warrant (i) outcomes, results, revenues or profits from the Counterparty's use of the Services; (ii) the accuracy or fitness of market data, third-party content, blockchain data or customer decisions; (iii) uninterrupted availability of third-party platforms or networks; or (iv) the outcome of investment, trading, custody or settlement activities. The Company's obligations are limited to activities permitted by its regulatory licences; if a licence is suspended or revoked such that the Services are no longer permitted, the Company may suspend performance without liability. The Company disclaims all implied warranties to the maximum extent permitted by law, including merchantability, fitness for purpose, accuracy and uninterrupted availability.
fallback: Reduced Warranties (Low-Risk). The Counterparty represents and warrants that: (a) it complies with Applicable Law; (b) the Services conform to this Agreement and do not infringe third-party rights; and (c) its personnel hold the required qualifications. The Counterparty shall provide evidence of authority and licences on request within [ten (10)] Business Days.
redflags:
Disclaimer of performance or conformity warranties for regulated, data, security or customer-facing services.
No warranty re malware, backdoors or undisclosed data collection.
License marked "pending", "conditional" or "restricted" and [Services] may fall outside scope.
Represents licensing but refuses evidence or confirmation [Services] within scope.
Subject to sanctions or owned/controlled by sanctioned persons.
Regulatory enforcement or AML/CFT investigation within twenty-four (24) months undisclosed.
[Company] asked to warrant outcomes or matters dependent on third parties, market or customer behavior.
usageNotes: Select variant based on [Company]'s role: Buy-Side Variant for [Company] as buyer procuring critical services (system integration, data processing, cybersecurity, payment, custody), regulated counterparties, transfers of customer data or digital assets, or high-value transactions (>USD 100,000 or >24 months); Baseline Clause for [Company] as buyer procuring non-critical, low-risk services; Sell-Side Variant for [Company] as supplier (must confirm services within [Company]'s regulatory license per Compliance Handbook and include license suspension carve-out). Buy-Side warranties for security (malware-free), regulatory licensing, sanctions/AML, data protection and insurance are non-negotiable for critical services, regulated counterparties, data processing and security-sensitive systems; counterparty resistance to these warranties requires immediate escalation to Head of Legal plus relevant stakeholder (Compliance for licensing/sanctions, CISO for security, DPO for data protection, CFO for insurance). Acceptable Fallback only for contracts <USD 50,000, <12 months, non-regulated, no customer data, no security-sensitive systems, established vendors. If uncertain which variant or whether to accept counterparty qualification, default to Buy-Side Variant and escalate. After completion, verify consistency with Service Levels, Limitation of Liability, Indemnity, Data Processing, IP and Termination clauses.
counselNotes: The reduced warranty set is acceptable only for low-value, low-risk contracts (e.g. value below [USD 50,000], term under [twelve (12)] months, non-regulated, no customer data or digital assets). Not acceptable for regulated services, digital assets, payment, customer-facing contracts, data processing or security-sensitive services.

title: DISCLAIMERS
purpose: Prevents unintended warranties and regulated advice.
baseline: Disclaimers. Save as expressly set out in this Agreement, and to the fullest extent permitted by law, all warranties, representations, conditions, undertakings and other terms, whether express or implied by statute, common law, custom, course of dealing or otherwise, are excluded, including any implied term as to satisfactory quality, merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, accuracy, completeness, non-infringement, reliability, timeliness, security or uninterrupted availability.
buyside: Disclaimer (Buy-Side Limits). No disclaimer or exclusion of warranties shall: (a) qualify, contradict or limit any express warranty, representation or undertaking given by the Counterparty in this Agreement; (b) extend to the Counterparty's obligations in respect of regulated services, data protection, information security, the Service Levels, Intellectual Property Rights or the indemnities; or (c) operate as a general exclusion of the Counterparty's obligations under this Agreement. To the extent a disclaimer purports to do any of the foregoing, it shall be of no effect.
sellside: Company Disclaimer (As Is). Save as expressly set out in this Agreement, the Company's Platform, Services and Documentation are provided on an "as is" and "as available" basis, and the Company does not warrant: (a) the accuracy, completeness, timeliness, fitness for purpose or performance of any market data, third-party service, blockchain network, exchange rate, settlement system or customer decision; (b) the uninterrupted or error-free availability of any third-party platform, API or network; (c) the outcome of any investment, trading, custody or asset-management activity; or (d) any results, revenues or savings arising from the Counterparty's use of the Services.
redflags:
Disclaimer that nullifies all warranties including those expressly given.
Disclaimer used to exclude breach of data, security or regulatory obligations.
Consumer-facing or regulated disclaimers that violate applicable consumer protection or financial services laws.
usageNotes: Disclaimers are subject to mandatory law in all [Company] jurisdictions. Courts may not uphold disclaimers that are unfair, unreasonable or contrary to public policy, particularly for consumer contracts.
counselNotes: Accept disclaimers only where the express warranties and obligations are preserved and the disclaimer does not negate the practical value of what was contracted.

title: INDEMNITIES
purpose: Allocates third-party and specified losses to the party controlling the risk.
buyside: Conduct of Claims and Enhanced Recovery. In addition to the Baseline, the Company may: (a) take, and require the Counterparty to cede, conduct of the defence and settlement of any claim subject to the indemnity, using counsel of the Company's choosing; (b) recover from the Counterparty all reasonable legal and investigation costs on a full-indemnity basis; and (c) recover any regulatory fine, penalty or sanction imposed on the Company to the extent attributable to the Counterparty's breach and recovery is permitted by applicable law and the Company's insurance.
sellside: Company Indemnity (Limited). The Company's sole indemnity is to indemnify the Counterparty against Losses arising from third-party claims that Company-provided materials infringe that third party's Intellectual Property Rights, such indemnity being (a) subject to Clause [●] (Limitation of Liability); and (b) excluding any Losses arising from the Counterparty's modification of the Company's materials, their combination with items not supplied by the Company, or any use outside the Permitted Purpose.
fallback: Third-Party-Claims Indemnity. The indemnity is limited to third-party claims, provided that: (a) the Company retains its right to recover direct losses through its breach-of-contract and termination remedies; and (b) the indemnity covers, as a minimum, infringement of Intellectual Property Rights, data breach, Security Incidents and breach of financial-crime laws.
redflags:
[Company] indemnifies counterparty for customer claims caused by counterparty conduct.
[Company] indemnifies counterparty for regulatory fines, penalties or enforcement costs arising from counterparty breach.
[Company] indemnifies counterparty for losses arising from counterparty negligence, fraud or wilful misconduct.
Indemnity is subject to a cap that applies to fraud, wilful misconduct or data breach.
usageNotes:
Full indemnity legal costs (solicitor-client basis) are recoverable in Singapore and certain other jurisdictions but not universally. Specify "full indemnity basis" in the clause where applicable.
Regulatory fines may not be insurable or indemnifiable in all jurisdictions. Verify with local counsel.
counselNotes: Where the counterparty resists a broad indemnity, a third-party-claims-only indemnity is acceptable provided the Company keeps its direct contractual remedies and the indemnity still covers IP infringement, data breach, Security Incident and financial-crime breach.

title: LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
purpose: Caps ordinary commercial liability while preserving critical carve-outs.
baseline:
Limitation of Liability. Subject to Clause [●] (Exclusions from Liability Cap), each Party's total aggregate liability to the other arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty or otherwise, shall not exceed the greater of:
(a) [USD X];
(b) the total Fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the [12] months immediately preceding the first event giving rise to the claim; and
(c) [where the liability arises from a single incident, USD Y].
buyside:
Buy-Side Cap. For critical services, or services involving data, security or regulated functions, the Counterparty's liability cap shall be:
(a) for general commercial claims, the greater of [12 months' Fees] and [USD X];
(b) for a data breach, Security Incident or loss of Customer Assets, [USD Y] (a super-cap); and
(c) uncapped in respect of fraud, wilful misconduct, the matters in Clause [●] (Exclusions from Liability Cap) and any liability that cannot be limited at law.
The Counterparty's cap shall not in any event be set below [USD X] for any contract involving Personal Data, security, regulated functions or Customer Assets.
sellside: Sell-Side Cap. The Company's total aggregate liability to the Counterparty arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of [USD X] and the Fees paid by the Counterparty in the [6] months immediately preceding the first event giving rise to the claim. Service credits are the Counterparty's sole financial remedy for SLA availability failures that do not constitute excluded liabilities under Clause [●] (Exclusions from Liability Cap).
fallback: Mutual Cap (Lower-Risk). The Parties may agree a mutual cap below 12 months' Fees, provided that: (a) the carve-outs in Clause [●] (Exclusions from Liability Cap) (including fraud, data breach, Intellectual Property Rights infringement and regulatory breach) are preserved in full; and (b) the cap is not set below [USD X] for any contract involving data, security, regulated functions or customer-facing services.
redflags:
Cap applies to fraud, wilful misconduct, data breach, IP infringement, regulatory breach, payment obligations or Customer Asset misuse.
Cap set at a level that is manifestly insufficient to cover realistic loss scenarios for high-risk services.
Mutual cap that applies equally even though Counterparty controls the highest risk activities.
usageNotes:
Liability caps are subject to reasonableness and public policy analysis under applicable law. Caps may be unenforceable in consumer contracts (Indonesia, Philippines) and for certain statutory obligations.
UCTA 1977 (Singapore) applies a reasonableness test to liability exclusions in business-to-business contracts.
counselNotes: Accept a mutual cap below 12 months' Fees only for lower-risk contracts, with the carve-outs preserved and a floor of [USD X] for data, security, regulated or customer-facing contracts.

title: EXCLUSIONS FROM LIABILITY CAP
purpose: Preserves remedies for non-ordinary risk.
buyside: Additional Carve-Outs (Critical Contracts). For critical buy-side contracts, each of the following is also excluded from any cap: (a) gross negligence; (b) abandonment of the Services or wilful failure to perform; (c) breach of tax-withholding obligations; and (d) breach of regulatory-cooperation obligations.
sellside: Symmetrical Application. The carve-outs in this Clause apply symmetrically to both Parties. The Counterparty shall not cap its liability for customer misuse of the Platform, breach of the licence or IP restrictions, breach of the acceptable-use policy, or misuse of the Company's Confidential Information.
fallback: Super-Cap in Lieu of Uncapped Liability. A super-cap (a higher monetary cap, rather than uncapped liability) may be agreed for: (a) a data breach, where the agreed amount is supported by available insurance; and (b) breach of confidentiality, where the agreed amount reflects realistic loss scenarios.
redflags:
No meaningful carve-outs — all claims subject to the general cap.
Fraud, wilful misconduct or Customer Asset loss subject to the general fee-based cap.
Carve-out for "gross negligence" removed by counterparty negotiation.
usageNotes: The list of carve-outs should be tailored to the specific risk profile of the contract. For digital asset, payment and custody contracts, Customer Asset loss and regulatory breach carve-outs are critical.
counselNotes: Never accept a cap on fraud, wilful misconduct, loss of Customer Assets or regulatory breach. A super-cap (not uncapped) may be accepted for data-breach and confidentiality-breach exposure only where it reflects realistic loss and available insurance.

title: CONSEQUENTIAL AND INDIRECT LOSS
purpose: Controls remote and speculative damages.
baseline: Consequential and Indirect Loss. Subject to Clause [●] (Exclusions from Liability Cap), neither Party shall be liable, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty or otherwise, for any of the following, in each case whether direct or indirect: loss of profit; loss of revenue; loss of goodwill; loss of anticipated savings; loss of business or business opportunity; business interruption; or trading loss. This exclusion does not apply to: (a) Losses falling within Clause [●] (Exclusions from Liability Cap); (b) Losses covered by an express indemnity in this Agreement; (c) breach of confidentiality, data-protection or information-security obligations; or (d) Losses arising from misuse of Customer Assets.
buyside: Preserved Direct Losses (Buy-Side). For the purposes of this Clause, the following are agreed to be recoverable direct losses and are not excluded as indirect or consequential loss: (a) the costs of data remediation and forensic investigation; (b) regulatory fines, penalties and enforcement costs attributable to the Counterparty's breach, to the extent recoverable at law; (c) the costs of procuring replacement services; (d) customer compensation or refunds caused by the Counterparty's breach; and (e) the cost of business interruption directly caused by a Service Level failure of the Counterparty.
sellside: Company Excluded Losses. Subject to Clause [●] (Exclusions from Liability Cap), the Company shall not be liable for: (a) loss of profit, revenue, anticipated savings, trading income, investment performance or business opportunity; (b) loss of data, Digital Assets or account balances arising from customer error, market conditions or third-party service failures; (c) business interruption caused by exchange outages, blockchain-network congestion, settlement-system failure or force majeure; or (d) indirect or derivative loss of any kind, howsoever arising.
redflags:
Exclusion removes core remedies for breach of data, security, asset or regulatory obligations.
"Consequential" or "indirect" used to characterise losses that are actually direct and foreseeable (e.g. data remediation costs, regulatory fines).
Exclusion applies even to losses explicitly covered by a named indemnity.
usageNotes: Courts in Singapore and Indonesia have interpreted "indirect" and "consequential" loss differently. Define clearly which categories of loss are excluded rather than relying on labels.
counselNotes: Accept a mutual consequential-loss exclusion only where direct losses are preserved for all key breach categories and remedies for data breach, Security Incident, IP infringement and regulatory breach are not removed.

title: INSURANCE
purpose: Provides financial backing for contractual risk.
sellside: Company Insurance. The Company makes no warranty that it maintains any specific level of insurance, and the existence of any Company insurance does not expand the Company's liability under this Agreement. The Counterparty is responsible for maintaining its own insurance appropriate to its obligations.
fallback: Reduced Insurance (Low-Risk). For low-risk, lower-value contracts, the Counterparty shall maintain insurance at commercially reasonable levels, including cyber and professional-indemnity cover, without being required to name the Company as additional insured.
redflags:
No cyber or errors and omissions insurance for technology, data or security vendors.
Insurance stated as sole remedy or cap on contractual liability.
No notice of cancellation or change obligation.
Insurance coverage below realistic loss scenarios for the risk profile.
usageNotes: Insurance availability and requirements vary by jurisdiction. Indonesian vendors may not maintain international-standard cyber coverage. Consider compensating contractual protections where insurance is inadequate.
counselNotes: The reduced insurance position is acceptable only for low-risk, lower-value contracts; for regulated, data-intensive or higher-value contracts apply the Baseline cover and Buy-Side terms.

title: AUDIT, INSPECTION, RECORDS AND REGULATORY ACCESS
purpose: Ensures evidence, verification and regulator-facing access.
baseline:
Audit, Inspection, Records and Regulatory Access. The Counterparty shall:
(a) keep complete, accurate and up-to-date records relating to its obligations under this Agreement, including financial, service, data-processing, security, personnel and compliance records;
(b) retain those records for at least [seven (7)] years after termination; and
(c) permit the Company, its authorised auditors and any Regulator to audit, inspect and verify compliance with this Agreement and Applicable Law on [thirty (30)] days' written notice, or immediately in the event of a Security Incident, suspected breach or Regulator request.
sellside: Company-Side Audit Limits. Where the Company is the supplier, audit rights are limited to: (a) verification of the Counterparty's compliance with the usage restrictions, licence scope, data obligations and security requirements; (b) an annual frequency on [thirty (30)] days' notice; and (c) confidentiality obligations protecting the Company's other customers' data.
fallback: Assurance-Report Audit (Low-Risk). For standard SaaS and low-risk contracts, an annual SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) report is accepted in lieu of a direct audit, and a direct audit right arises only on a Security Incident, suspected breach or Regulator request.
redflags:
No audit rights for critical, regulated or data-intensive services.
Regulator access blocked, delayed or subject to counterparty consent.
Audit limited to self-certification without third-party verification rights.
Records retention period too short for regulatory or litigation purposes.
usageNotes: MAS TRM Guidelines require direct regulator access for critical outsourced functions. OJK and BAPPEBTI have equivalent requirements. Do not accept contracts that limit or block direct regulator access.
counselNotes: Accept the assurance-report approach only for standard SaaS / low-risk contracts; retain full audit and Regulator-access rights for regulated, critical or data-intensive services.

title: REPORTING OBLIGATIONS
purpose: Requires operational, compliance and incident reporting.
baseline: Reporting Obligations. The Counterparty shall provide the Company with reports at the frequency and in the format specified in Schedule [●] (Reporting), including: (a) monthly SLA and KPI performance reports; (b) incident and security reports within the timelines in Clause [●] (Security Incident and Data Breach Notification); (c) reconciliation reports for Customer Assets or financial flows; (d) compliance and regulatory-status reports; and (e) subcontractor lists and changes.
buyside: Enhanced Reporting. For regulated, customer-facing or critical services, the Counterparty shall also provide: (a) real-time alerts and dashboards for critical operational events; (b) a root-cause analysis within [five (5)] Business Days of any material incident; (c) regulatory and compliance certifications on a [quarterly / annual] basis; and (d) immediate reporting of any material adverse change affecting its ability to perform.
sellside: Company Reporting. The Company's reporting is limited to what is expressly agreed in the applicable Service Levels or Schedule. No reporting obligation requires the Company to disclose information that is commercially sensitive, legally privileged or confidential to its other customers.
fallback: Quarterly Reporting (Lower-Risk). For non-critical, lower-risk engagements, reporting may be provided quarterly, provided that incident reporting, material compliance-breach reporting and material-change notification are provided as and when they arise.
redflags:
No reporting for SLA failures, incidents, asset reconciliation or regulated services.
Reporting obligations so vague or infrequent as to provide no meaningful oversight.
usageNotes: Reporting requirements should be operationally executable. Agree formats and frequencies with relevant internal teams before including in contract.
counselNotes: Quarterly reporting is acceptable for non-critical engagements, but incident, material-compliance-breach and material-change reporting must always be provided promptly.

title: CHANGE CONTROL
purpose: Controls amendments to scope, costs, systems or obligations.
baseline: Change Control. No change to the Services, the Fees, the Service Levels, data flows, security architecture, subcontractors, regulatory responsibilities, integration design, operational dependencies or any other material obligation is binding unless agreed in a written change order signed by authorised representatives of both Parties. The Company may reject any proposed change, and the Counterparty shall not implement any change that has not been approved in writing.
buyside: Change-Order Requirements. Each change-order request shall set out: (a) a description of the proposed change and its impact on the Services, the Fees, timelines and the Service Levels; (b) its impact on data flows, security, compliance and regulatory obligations; (c) the Company's engineering and security review where the change is technically material; and (d) Legal review and approval before signature.
sellside: Company Platform Changes. The Company may make non-material changes to the Platform (including updates, bug fixes and security patches) without the Counterparty's consent, provided they do not materially degrade the core functionality of the Services. The Company shall give the Counterparty [thirty (30)] days' advance notice of any material platform change.
fallback: Operational Change Notices. Operational change notices (without a formal change order) are permitted only for: (a) administrative changes (such as contact details or notice addresses); and (b) minor technical updates with no legal, commercial or security impact.
redflags:
Counterparty can change service scope, location, data processing, security controls or subcontractors unilaterally.
Email side deals or informal changes treated as binding amendments.
Counterparty can change pricing, SLAs or terms by posting updated online policies.
usageNotes: All change orders must go through Legal for review, regardless of how "minor" the business team characterises them. Changes to data flows, security architecture or regulatory scope require compliance sign-off.

title: SUSPENSION RIGHTS
purpose: Allows [Company] to stop activity where risk arises.
baseline: Suspension Rights. The Company may immediately suspend access, performance, payment of Fees or any affected Services, without prior notice and without liability, where it determines that suspension is necessary to prevent or mitigate: (a) a Security Incident or data-breach risk; (b) a breach of Applicable Law or Regulatory Requirements; (c) an AML/CFT, sanctions or financial-crime risk; (d) a risk to Customer Assets; (e) fraud or suspected fraud; or (f) a material risk to the Company's operational integrity, reputation or regulatory standing. The Company shall notify the Counterparty of the suspension as soon as reasonably practicable and shall lift it once the risk has been remediated.
buyside: No Liability for Good-Faith Suspension. The Company shall not be liable for any loss, cost, damage or claim arising from a suspension made in good faith. The right to suspend is in addition to, and does not limit, any other right or remedy available to the Company.
sellside: Company Suspension (Counterparty Use). The Company may immediately suspend the Counterparty's access to the Platform, API or Services for: (a) non-payment of undisputed Fees outstanding for more than [thirty (30)] days; (b) a security threat, breach or unauthorised access; (c) breach of the acceptable-use policy or usage limits; (d) legal, regulatory or compliance risk; or (e) the Counterparty's insolvency, sanctions designation or regulatory investigation. The Company shall give notice of suspension where operationally practicable.
fallback: Notice-and-Cure Before Suspension. For non-critical commercial breaches (other than security, regulatory, financial-crime or Customer-Asset matters), the Company shall give notice and a cure period not exceeding [five (5)] Business Days before suspending.
redflags:
No suspension right for security incidents, regulatory risk, sanctions or Customer Asset risk.
[Company] required to give advance notice before suspending for security incidents — creates dangerous delay.
Suspension limited to circumstances where [Company] can prove actual loss.
usageNotes: Suspension rights are a critical risk-management tool. Do not accept restrictions that prevent [Company] from acting immediately when security, regulatory or customer asset risk arises.
counselNotes: Notice-and-cure before suspension is acceptable only for non-critical commercial breaches; the Company must retain immediate suspension rights for security, regulatory, financial-crime, fraud and Customer-Asset risks.

title: TERMINATION FOR CAUSE
purpose: Provides exit for breach and non-performance.
buyside: Additional Company Termination Triggers. In addition to the Baseline, the Company may terminate immediately for: (a) chronic failure to meet Critical Service Levels in any [three (3)] consecutive months; (b) failure to maintain required insurance, licences or regulatory authorisations; (c) unauthorised subcontracting of regulated, data or security functions; (d) a change of control of the Counterparty to a Company competitor or sanctioned entity; or (e) any other event that, in the Company's reasonable judgement, creates material regulatory, security or operational risk.
sellside: Company Termination (Supplier). The Company may terminate this Agreement for cause on [thirty (30)] days' written notice for: (a) the Counterparty's persistent failure to pay undisputed amounts after demand; (b) the Counterparty's breach of the permitted-use or IP restrictions; or (c) any other material breach not remedied within the notice period.
redflags:
No immediate termination right for security incidents, data breach, regulatory breach, sanctions or Customer Asset misuse.
Cure period applies to fraud, wilful misconduct or irremediable breach.
Termination requires mutual consent or arbitration award before it is effective.
usageNotes: Termination rights must be operationally executable. Test the mechanism before signing: can Legal send the notice, is the correct entity identified, and what happens to Customer Assets and data on termination?
counselNotes: A [thirty (30)]-day cure period is acceptable for non-critical, remediable commercial breaches; fraud, sanctions, data breach, regulatory breach, insolvency, misuse of Customer Assets and IP infringement must remain immediate-termination triggers with no cure.

title: TERMINATION FOR CONVENIENCE
purpose: Provides strategic exit right.
baseline: Termination for Convenience. The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving [30 / 60 / 90] days' written notice to the Counterparty. On such termination, the Company's sole obligation is to pay undisputed Fees for Services properly performed up to the termination date, and the Company shall not be liable for any other loss, cost or damage arising from a termination for convenience.
buyside: Buy-Side Convenience Rights. The Company shall have a termination-for-convenience right exercisable on [thirty (30)] days' notice for non-critical services, and [sixty (60)] days' notice for critical or operationally complex services, with no early-termination fee, break fee, minimum committed fees or wind-down costs unless expressly agreed and approved by Finance.
sellside: Convenience Rights (Company as Supplier). Where the Company is the supplier: (a) the Company may terminate for convenience on [thirty (30)] days' written notice; (b) the Counterparty may terminate for convenience on [ninety (90)] days' written notice; and (c) the Counterparty shall pay all Fees committed and properly invoiced up to the end of its notice period.
fallback: Mutual Convenience Termination (Non-Critical). For non-critical contracts, either Party may terminate for convenience on [sixty (60)] days' notice, provided that: (a) no early-termination fee applies; and (b) transition-assistance rights are preserved for the notice period.
redflags:
No termination for convenience in long-term critical vendor contract without performance remedies.
Termination for convenience triggers large early termination fee, minimum committed fees or lock-in penalty.
Notice period for convenience termination exceeds [90] days without [Company] business justification.
usageNotes: Check exit rights before signing any multi-year contract. Termination for convenience is the primary protection against long-term vendor lock-in.

title: TERMINATION FOR REGULATORY REASON
purpose: Allows exit where continuation is unlawful or regulator-sensitive.
baseline: Termination for Regulatory Reason. The Company may terminate this Agreement immediately without liability if, in its reasonable opinion, continuation would or might: (a) breach Applicable Law or Regulatory Requirements applicable to the Company; (b) breach its licence conditions or a Regulator's expectations; (c) breach applicable sanctions, AML/CFT or financial-crime requirements; (d) compromise the Company's internal compliance standards; or (e) adversely affect the Company's regulatory standing, licence or product approvals. On such termination, the Company's obligations are limited to payment of undisputed Fees for Services properly performed up to the termination date.
buyside: Nature of the Regulatory Termination Right. The regulatory termination right shall be: (a) unilateral, not requiring the Counterparty's consent; (b) effective immediately on notice; (c) without penalty, break fee or liability; and (d) supported by transition assistance from the Counterparty for [ninety (90)] days after termination.
sellside: Regulatory Termination (Company as Supplier). Where the Company is the supplier, it may terminate or modify the Services immediately where: (a) a change in law, regulatory guidance or its licence conditions makes the Services impracticable or unlawful; or (b) the Counterparty's use of the Services creates legal or regulatory risk for the Company.
fallback: Notice-and-Consultation (Non-Imminent Risk). Where the regulatory risk is not imminent and does not require emergency action, the Company shall give notice and consult with the Counterparty before terminating for regulatory reason.
redflags:
Counterparty consent required before [Company] can terminate for regulatory risk.
Regulatory termination triggers penalties, break fees or committed payment obligations.
No transition assistance following regulatory termination.
usageNotes: Regulatory termination rights must be preserved unconditionally for all regulated entity contracts. Regulators in Singapore, Indonesia and Philippines may impose fast-acting obligations that require immediate contract exit.
counselNotes: Use notice-and-consultation only where the regulatory risk is not imminent; retain the immediate regulatory termination right for urgent or emergency situations.

title: TERMINATION FOR SECURITY INCIDENT OR DATA BREACH
purpose: Provides exit for cyber and data risk.
baseline: Termination for Security Incident or Data Breach. The Company may terminate this Agreement immediately by written notice if: (a) a Security Incident or breach of Personal Data materially affects the Company, its End Users, Personal Data, Customer Assets, systems or regulated operations; or (b) the Counterparty fails to notify the Company in accordance with Clause [●] (Security Incident and Data Breach Notification), or fails to remediate a Security Incident to the Company's reasonable satisfaction within [thirty (30)] days. The Counterparty shall cooperate fully with forensic investigation and regulatory notification following termination.
buyside: Investigation and Evidence Preservation. The Company may suspend access and initiate a forensic investigation before deciding whether to terminate. The Counterparty shall: (a) not delete, alter or destroy any evidence relating to the Security Incident without the Company's written consent; (b) cooperate with the Company's appointed forensic investigators; and (c) bear all costs of investigation, notification and remediation attributable to its systems or conduct.
sellside: Security Suspension or Termination (Company as Supplier). The Company may terminate or suspend the Counterparty's access immediately if the Counterparty's systems, personnel or integrations create a security threat to the Company's Platform or Customer Assets, including unauthorised access attempts, credential compromise or suspicious transaction patterns.
fallback: Cure Period (Minor Incidents). A [thirty (30)]-day cure period applies to minor security incidents that do not affect customer data, Customer Assets or regulated systems, and do not require regulatory notification.
redflags:
No termination right until final legal determination of breach — delays response unacceptably.
Evidence destruction permitted before investigation is complete.
No forensic cooperation obligation post-termination.
usageNotes: Cyber incidents require fast action. Termination and suspension rights must be usable within hours, not days. Pre-agree escalation and response protocols with Security and Legal before contracts go live.
counselNotes: A cure period is acceptable only for minor incidents with no customer-data, Customer-Asset, regulated-system or regulatory-notification impact; otherwise the immediate termination right applies.

title: TERMINATION FOR INSOLVENCY, CHANGE OF CONTROL, SANCTIONS, ILLEGALITY OR REPUTATIONAL RISK
purpose: Protects against counterparty deterioration and adverse control changes.
buyside: Change-of-Control Notification. In addition: (a) the Counterparty shall notify the Company immediately of any proposed Change of Control; (b) the Company shall have [thirty (30)] days from receipt of that notice to exercise its termination right; (c) the notice shall include full details of the acquirer, the acquiring entity, the ownership structure and its regulatory status; and (d) the Counterparty shall bear all transition costs where termination is triggered by a Change of Control.
sellside: Insolvency/Sanctions Termination (Company as Supplier). The Company may terminate for the Counterparty's insolvency or sanctions designation without liability, and the Counterparty shall have no claim against the Company for loss of anticipated profits, sunk costs or break fees following such termination.
fallback: Mutual Insolvency Termination. Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately if the other becomes insolvent, is unable to pay its debts as they fall due, or enters any analogous insolvency process.
redflags:
No termination right on counterparty change of control — creates risk of contract with [Company] competitor or sanctioned entity.
Sanctions designation not an immediate termination event.
Counterparty acquired by competitor with no [Company] exit right.
usageNotes: Change of control provisions are critical for long-term or strategic contracts. Ensure change of control is defined broadly to include economic control, not just legal ownership changes.
counselNotes: Accept mutual insolvency termination rights. Resist any broad, subjective reputational-risk termination against the Company unless it is mutual, objective (tied to specified triggers) and subject to a notice-and-cure period.

title: CONSEQUENCES OF TERMINATION
purpose: Preserves accrued rights and manages post-termination obligations.
sellside:
Upon termination or expiry of [Counterparty]'s access rights, [Counterparty] shall:
(a) immediately cease all use of [Company]'s [Platform], APIs and [Confidential Information];
(b) delete all [Company] materials from [Counterparty]'s systems and provide written confirmation; and
(c) pay all outstanding undisputed [Fees].
fallback: Accept a [60]-day transition period for complex operational handover, provided services continue at current [Service Levels] during the transition.
redflags:
Termination releases counterparty from pre-termination breach obligations.
No data return or deletion obligation on termination.
Accrued indemnity, liability, audit or regulatory obligations extinguished on termination.
usageNotes: Termination mechanics must be operationally planned in advance for critical services. Include a termination checklist as a Schedule for complex arrangements.

title: EXIT ASSISTANCE, TRANSITION, MIGRATION AND DATA RETURN
purpose: Prevents lock-in and service disruption.
sellside: [Company] will provide [Counterparty] with standard data export functionality and migration support as part of the [Service] at the conclusion of the [Term], subject to applicable technical, security and legal limitations. Extended or bespoke migration support is available at [Company]'s published professional services rates.
fallback:
Accept paid exit assistance for ordinary services, provided:
(a) [Counterparty] cannot impose proprietary lock-in or block data access during transition; and
(b) rates for exit assistance are pre-agreed in the contract.
redflags:
No data export or migration capability — proprietary format lock-in.
Data deleted before migration is complete.
Exit assistance conditioned on payment of disputed amounts or waiver of claims.
Exit fees disproportionate or designed to deter exit.
usageNotes: Plan exit before signing. For SaaS and critical platform dependencies, validate export format, data completeness and migration feasibility with Engineering before contract execution.

title: FORCE MAJEURE
purpose: Allocates risk for events beyond reasonable control without excusing payment or preventable failures.
baseline:
No Party shall be liable for delay or failure to perform its obligations under this [Agreement] to the extent caused by a [Force Majeure Event] beyond its reasonable control, provided that:
(a) the affected Party gives written notice to the other Party promptly and no later than [5] business days after the [Force Majeure Event] arises, specifying the nature and expected duration;
(b) the affected Party takes all reasonable steps to mitigate the impact and resume performance as soon as practicable; and
(c) the affected Party continues to perform all obligations not affected by the [Force Majeure Event].
Force majeure shall not excuse:
(d) payment obligations accrued before the [Force Majeure Event];
(e) confidentiality, data protection, security, [Customer Asset] safeguarding or regulatory cooperation obligations; or
(f) obligations where the [Force Majeure Event] was foreseeable and preventable by the affected Party.
buyside:
For buy-side contracts involving critical services, add:
(a) [Counterparty]'s force majeure rights are limited where the event was caused or contributed to by [Counterparty]'s inadequate security controls, single points of failure or inadequate BCP;
(b) if a [Force Majeure Event] continues for more than [30] days, [Company] may terminate immediately without liability; and
(c) data, customer asset safeguarding and regulatory obligations continue regardless of force majeure.
sellside: [Company] is not responsible for force majeure events affecting third-party infrastructure, blockchain networks, exchange platforms, payment networks, settlement systems or cloud service providers. [Counterparty] accepts these risks where the [Services] depend on third-party infrastructure outside [Company]'s control.
fallback:
Accept mutual force majeure with:
(a) clear notice requirement (not less than [5] business days);
(b) mitigation obligation; and
(c) termination right if the event continues for more than [30/60] days.
redflags:
Force majeure excuses payment obligations, data breach liability, asset safeguarding obligations or regulatory cooperation.
Force majeure defined so broadly as to cover normal business risk, market downturns or supply chain issues.
No notice or mitigation obligation.
No termination right if event is prolonged.
usageNotes: Cyber incidents are generally not force majeure events where adequate security controls were not in place. Expressly exclude cyber incidents caused by counterparty negligence from force majeure.

title: MATERIAL ADVERSE CHANGE
purpose: Allows response to material deterioration in counterparty or transaction risk.
buyside: For long-term, critical or strategic contracts, include financial covenants requiring [Counterparty] to maintain minimum financial ratios or metrics and to notify [Company] immediately of any event that triggers or is likely to trigger an MAC.
sellside:
[Company] does not accept broad subjective MAC termination rights against [Company] by [Counterparty]. Any MAC termination right against [Company] must be:
(a) objective and limited to specific defined events; and
(b) subject to a [30]-day notice and cure period.
fallback: For shorter-term or lower-risk contracts, MAC provisions may be limited to insolvency, sanctions and regulatory licence loss.
redflags:
Broad subjective MAC right exercisable by counterparty against [Company] without objective conditions.
MAC defined so broadly as to cover ordinary market conditions, regulatory changes or strategic business decisions.
usageNotes: MAC provisions are most common in M&A transactions, financing arrangements and long-term strategic contracts. For ordinary vendor contracts, insolvency, sanctions and regulatory loss provisions are generally sufficient.

title: CHANGE IN LAW
purpose: Allocates cost and operational impact of legal and regulatory changes.
baseline:
If a change in [Applicable Laws] or [Regulatory Requirements] after the [Effective Date] materially affects a Party's ability to perform its obligations under this [Agreement], the Parties shall promptly discuss and agree necessary amendments.
[Company] may terminate this [Agreement] without liability, penalty or break fee where:
(a) continuation would be unlawful or contrary to [Regulatory Requirements] applicable to [Company];
(b) continuation would be commercially impracticable for [Company]; or
(c) the required amendments cannot be agreed within [60] days.
buyside: The cost of complying with changes in law applicable to [Counterparty]'s business, personnel, systems or services shall be borne by [Counterparty]. [Company] shall not bear compliance costs for obligations that apply to [Counterparty] as a matter of law.
sellside:
Where a change in law materially and demonstrably increases [Company]'s cost of providing the [Services], [Company] may:
(a) notify [Counterparty] of the impact and proposed fee adjustment; and
(b) if [Counterparty] does not agree to the adjustment within [30] days, terminate on [60] days' notice.
fallback: Accept equitable cost adjustment for changes in law that impose materially new and verifiable obligations on both Parties, where the scope and cost are agreed and documented.
redflags:
[Company] required to bear compliance costs for laws applicable to counterparty's own business.
Change in law termination requires counterparty consent or is not permitted.
usageNotes: Monitor legislative and regulatory pipelines in Indonesia, Singapore, Philippines and India for changes affecting [Company] group contracts. Flag relevant changes to Head of Legal.

title: ASSIGNMENT, NOVATION, TRANSFER AND CHANGE OF CONTROL
purpose: Controls transfer of rights and obligations.
baseline:
Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, sub-licence or otherwise deal with its rights or obligations under this [Agreement] without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that [Company] may assign or transfer its rights and obligations to:
(a) a [Company] [Affiliate];
(b) a successor entity following a merger, reorganisation or transfer of all or substantially all of [Company]'s business to which this [Agreement] relates; or
(c) as required in connection with financing, securitisation or group restructuring.
Any purported assignment in breach of this Clause is void.
buyside:
In addition:
(a) [Counterparty] shall not assign or transfer to a [Company] competitor, a sanctioned entity, or an entity that creates legal, regulatory or reputational risk for [Company];
(b) a [Change of Control] of [Counterparty] shall be treated as an assignment requiring [Company]'s consent; and
(c) [Company] may withhold consent to any assignment where [Company] determines, in its reasonable judgment, that the proposed assignee does not meet [Company]'s due diligence, regulatory or security standards.
sellside: [Company] may assign or transfer its rights and obligations to any [Company] entity or any successor as part of a group reorganisation without consent. [Counterparty] shall not assign, transfer, novate or subcontract its obligations without [Company]'s prior written consent.
fallback: Accept assignment to existing [Company] affiliates or intra-group restructuring without consent. Accept counterparty assignment to a non-competitor that demonstrates equivalent capability and creditworthiness, subject to [Company]'s right to conduct due diligence.
redflags:
Counterparty may freely assign to a [Company] competitor, offshore entity, insolvent affiliate or unvetted subcontractor.
Restrictions on [Company] group assignment that prevent legitimate reorganisation or financing.
usageNotes: Assignment clauses are particularly important for data processing, regulated services and customer-facing arrangements where the identity of the counterparty is material.

title: RELATIONSHIP OF PARTIES; NO PARTNERSHIP, AGENCY OR FIDUCIARY DUTY
purpose: Prevents unintended authority or regulated characterisation.
baseline: The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this [Agreement] creates or is intended to create a partnership, joint venture, employment relationship, agency, trust, fiduciary relationship, association, or any authority for either Party to bind, represent or act on behalf of the other Party, unless expressly stated.
sellside: [Company] does not provide investment advice, financial planning, tax advice, custodial services, brokerage, dealing, trust services, fiduciary services or any other regulated or advisory service to [Counterparty] through this [Agreement] unless expressly and separately agreed and licensed.
fallback: For referral, marketing and introducer arrangements, add express limitations on [Counterparty]'s authority to make regulated statements, financial promotions or product claims on behalf of [Company].
redflags:
Counterparty may act as [Company] agent or bind [Company] without express written controls.
Agreement creates de facto fiduciary duty, trust or investment management relationship by conduct.
usageNotes: For regulated financial services, the relationship characterisation affects licensing and regulatory perimeter. Always involve Compliance and Legal before signing arrangements where Counterparty interacts with customers on [Company]'s behalf.

title: NOTICES
purpose: Ensures legally effective communications.
buyside:
All formal notices (including breach notices, termination notices, claims and regulatory notices) shall be copied to:
[Company] Legal: [legal@[company-domain] or as updated by [Company]]
[Counterparty]'s General Counsel or Legal Department: [address]
Notices sent to business contacts only (without Legal copy) shall not be effective for formal breach, termination or claim purposes.
sellside: [Company] may issue operational notices (including SLA reports, invoices, product updates and non-material communications) by email to [Counterparty]'s designated operational contact. Formal breach, termination, indemnity and regulatory notices require the formal notice procedure above.
fallback: Accept email notices for ordinary communications. Require copy to Legal for all notices of breach, termination, claim or regulatory matter.
redflags:
Notice only to business user without Legal copy for termination, breach or claim.
Notice sent to personal email, informal channel or outdated address.
Deemed notice rules that make notice effective before actual delivery (e.g. 3 days after posting to a disputed address).
usageNotes: Include Legal as a mandatory copy recipient for all formal notices in every contract. Ensure notice addresses are updated each time personnel changes.

title: ENTIRE AGREEMENT
purpose: Prevents reliance on prior statements outside the contract.
baseline:
This [Agreement] constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, proposals, negotiations, representations, warranties and communications, whether oral or written, relating to its subject matter.
Each Party acknowledges that it has not relied on any representation, warranty or statement not expressly set out in this [Agreement] in entering into it, except that this Clause does not limit or exclude liability for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation.
buyside: [Company] has not relied on any product claims, technology performance guarantees, regulatory assurances, feasibility statements, reference implementations or marketing materials provided by [Counterparty] that are not expressly included in this [Agreement]. Any such representations shall be documented in a Schedule or warranty in this [Agreement] before signing.
sellside: [Counterparty] has not relied on any representations by [Company] about anticipated usage volumes, revenue projections, customer acquisition, market performance or business outcomes that are not expressly stated in this [Agreement].
fallback:
Accept standard entire agreement clause if:
(a) fraud carve-out is preserved; and
(b) all agreed business terms are documented in the contract before signing.
redflags:
Counterparty relies on sales representations, pitch materials, demos or external statements not in the contract.
No fraud carve-out — entire agreement clause used to exclude liability for pre-contractual misrepresentation.
usageNotes: Before signing, ensure all agreed commercial terms (pricing, service scope, SLA, milestones, key personnel) are documented in the Agreement or a Schedule. Do not rely on email side arrangements.

title: AMENDMENTS AND VARIATIONS
purpose: Prevents informal or unauthorised contract changes.
baseline: No amendment, modification, variation, waiver or supplementation of this [Agreement] is valid or binding unless made in writing and signed by an authorised representative of each Party. No act, omission, conduct or course of dealing shall constitute an amendment or waiver unless documented in accordance with this Clause.
buyside:
